findings.claim: Reich and Ruiperez-Valiente analysed every HarvardX and MITx course on edX from launch to May 2018.
findings.number: 565 course iterations, 261 courses, 12.67 million registrations, 5.63 million learners
findings.effect_size_or_detail: Covers two of the largest edX course providers only; the authors say data from other providers might differ.
findings.source_name: Reich and Ruiperez-Valiente, The MOOC Pivot, Science 363(6423):130-131 (2019), author postprint

findings.claim: Completion among all participants (registered and viewed the course) fell over time and never improved.
findings.effect_size_or_detail: 2017-18: 30,650 completions of 980,589 participants. The authors: low completion 'has not budged in six years'.
findings.source_name: The MOOC Pivot, Table S3

findings.claim: Even learners who paid for the verified track completed only about half the time.
findings.effect_size_or_detail: Learners who said on a survey they intended to complete: 15.42% completed in 2017-18.
findings.source_name: The MOOC Pivot, Table S3

findings.claim: About half of registrants never opened the course, and per-course certification was very low.
findings.number: 52% never enter the courseware; per-course certified share mean 5.03%, median 2.88% (N = 565 courses)
findings.effect_size_or_detail: Per-course percentage participating: mean 48.02%.
findings.source_name: The MOOC Pivot, main text and Table S4

findings.claim: Most learners never came back after their first year.
findings.number: Only 12% of the largest cohort (2015-16, 1.1 million learners) took another course the next year; second-year retention fell from 38% (first cohort) to 7% (2016-17 cohort)
findings.effect_size_or_detail: Table S1 gives 37.5% for 2012-13 to 2013-14 and 9.98% for 2016-17 to 2017-18; the text's 7% figure and the table do not match exactly, so cite the table.
findings.source_name: The MOOC Pivot, main text and Table S1

findings.claim: Certificates went mainly to learners in the richest countries; learners in low-HDI countries earned very few.
findings.number: 2017-18: very-high-HDI countries had 55.58% of enrolments and 68.7% of certifications; low-HDI countries had 3.2% of enrolments and 1.43% of certifications
findings.effect_size_or_detail: The authors conclude that MOOCs are 'primarily a complementary asset' for learners already inside existing education systems, and that providers are heading towards 'already-affluent, already-educated learners'.
findings.source_name: The MOOC Pivot, Table S2 and main text

findings.claim: MOOC providers pivoted to paywalls and paid online professional master's degrees.
findings.number: Examples cited: a $21,000 online master's in accounting (Indiana) and a $22,000 online MBA (Illinois)
findings.effect_size_or_detail: edX began building paywalls in May 2018 and in October 2018 was the last major provider to announce online master's degree partnerships.
findings.source_name: The MOOC Pivot, main text

findings.claim: Harvard and MIT sold edX to the for-profit 2U. 2U then filed for Chapter 11.
findings.number: $800 million (2021); 2U shares fell 86% soon after the sale; debt of nearly $950 million before restructuring
findings.effect_size_or_detail: Harvard and MIT put the sale proceeds into a nonprofit, Axim Collaborative (launched spring 2023).
findings.source_name: The Harvard Crimson, 27 July 2024

findings.claim: Coursera is a public company. Its 2025 revenue came from consumer subscriptions and certificates, enterprise sales and degrees.
findings.number: 2025 revenue $757.5M (up 9%); 197 million registered learners at 31 Dec 2025; 1,730 paid enterprise customers
findings.effect_size_or_detail: Coursera says its registered-learner count 'is not intended as a measure of active engagement'. 2025 consumer revenue was $502.2M and enterprise revenue was $255.3M.
findings.source_name: Coursera Q4 and Full Year 2025 Earnings Release

findings.claim: Coursera agreed to combine with Udemy in an all-stock deal aimed at workforce reskilling.
findings.number: Implied combined equity value about $2.5 billion; 0.800 Coursera shares per Udemy share; 59%/41% ownership; pro forma revenue above $1.5 billion
findings.effect_size_or_detail: Announced 17 December 2025. Completion in 2026 is reported only in secondary news, which I did not open.
findings.source_name: SEC Form 425 filed by Coursera (press release exhibit)

findings.claim: OpenStax reports large cumulative savings for students.
findings.number: $3.8B saved all-time; $374.3M annually; 49M students reached all-time; 5.4M annually; used by 71% of US colleges and universities annually
findings.effect_size_or_detail: These are OpenStax's own figures and the page does not give its method. 'Annually' refers to an unnamed current year. The page also claims a 65x social ROI.
findings.source_name: OpenStax Impact page

findings.claim: Hilton's 2016 review found that OER produce the same learning outcomes while saving students money.
findings.number: 16 studies synthesised
findings.effect_size_or_detail: Students 'generally' reach the same learning outcomes with OER and save a considerable amount of money; students and faculty are generally positive about OER.
findings.source_name: Hilton, ETR&D 64(4):573-590 (2016), abstract

findings.claim: Hilton's 2020 follow-up review covers efficacy and perceptions studies published 2015-2018.
findings.number: 16 efficacy studies and 20 perceptions studies
findings.effect_size_or_detail: I could read only the partial abstract on ERIC, which contains the study counts. The full findings are not confirmed here.
findings.source_name: Hilton, ETR&D (2020), ERIC EJ1256283

findings.claim: At the University of Georgia, course grades rose and DFW rates fell after the same instructors switched to OER.
findings.number: 21,822 students, 8 courses, 13 semesters; DFW 10.87% to 8.19%; A grades 17.96% to 23.46%; A- 11.33% to 19.06%
findings.effect_size_or_detail: Larger gains for Pell recipients (DFW 14.56% to 10.13%; average grade up 10.98% vs 6.90% for non-Pell) and for non-White students (DFW 15.28% to 10.15%; average grade 2.525 to 2.857). The design is a non-randomised pre/post comparison at one university with instructors held constant. The authors note the OER switch may have triggered other teaching changes, often with help from UGA's teaching centre.
findings.source_name: Colvard, Watson and Park, IJTLHE 30(2):262-276 (2018)

findings.claim: CLEP offers 34 exams at $97 each, plus any test-centre or remote-proctoring fees.
findings.number: 34 exams; $97 per exam
findings.effect_size_or_detail: History and social sciences 12, composition and literature 6, science and mathematics 7, business 5, world languages 4.
findings.source_name: College Board, CLEP Exams

findings.claim: ACE recommends a passing score of 50 on each CLEP exam and assigns 3 to 12 semester hours per exam.
findings.number: Score 50; 3 hours for most exams, 4 for Calculus, 6 for Composition, English Literature, Biology, Chemistry, Natural Sciences, and Social Sciences and History; language Level 2 up to 9 or 12 hours
findings.effect_size_or_detail: Each college sets its own policy on which exams it accepts and how much credit it grants.
findings.source_name: College Board, ACE Credit Recommendations

findings.claim: Students who place out of an introductory course with CLEP do as well as or better than peers in the next course. They are also rare in the sample.
findings.number: Subsequent-course grade differences favouring CLEP students of 0.11 to 0.82 GPA points; not significant for Calculus, College Mathematics and French
findings.effect_size_or_detail: CLEP groups are tiny next to comparison groups (for example, College Composition 47 CLEP vs 29,592 non-CLEP; US History I 43 vs 17,565; largest is Spanish at 273). The study is observational and self-selected, and it covers only recent high-school graduates at 5 to 28 four-year institutions per exam.
findings.source_name: Feng and Wyatt, The Validity of CLEP Scores for Course Placement Decisions, College Board Research (May 2025)

findings.claim: In a Harvard introductory physics course, a carefully designed GPT-4 tutor beat in-class active learning on immediate post-tests.
findings.number: Post-test median 4.5 (AI) vs 3.5 (in class), pre-test median 2.75; effect size 0.63 SD by linear regression, 0.73 to 1.3 SD by quantile regression
findings.effect_size_or_detail: 194 students, crossover RCT over two weeks (weeks 9-10, Fall 2023). Median AI time on task was 49 min, against an assumed 60 min in class. Engagement 4.1 vs 3.6 and motivation 3.4 vs 3.1 on 5-point scales. The tutor followed a system prompt built on pedagogy, scaffolded problems step by step and used pre-written expert solutions rather than GPT-4 alone. The authors say accuracy relied on those pre-written answers and the result may not hold for higher-order tasks. The tests were narrow and given immediately after the lesson.
findings.source_name: Kestin et al., AI tutoring outperforms in-class active learning, Scientific Reports 15:17458 (2025)

findings.claim: Unrestricted GPT-4 raised practice scores but lowered exam scores once access was removed. A guarded tutor version largely avoided the harm.
findings.number: Practice: +48% (GPT Base), +127% (GPT Tutor). After access was removed: -17% for GPT Base vs control
findings.effect_size_or_detail: Nearly 1,000 high-school maths students in a field experiment. GPT Tutor used prompts designed to safeguard learning, and its negative effects were 'largely mitigated'. The authors attribute the harm to students using the tool as a crutch.
findings.source_name: Bastani et al., Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning, PNAS 122 (2025), abstract via RePEc

findings.claim: AI guidance given to human tutors in real time raised student mastery, most of all for weaker tutors, at low cost.
findings.number: +4 percentage points mastery (p<0.01); +9 pp for students of lower-rated tutors; about $20 per tutor per year
findings.effect_size_or_detail: RCT with 900 tutors and 1,800 K-12 students from historically underserved communities. A human stays in the loop; the AI supports the tutor rather than replacing them.
findings.source_name: Wang, Ribeiro, Robinson, Loeb and Demszky, Tutor CoPilot, arXiv 2410.03017

findings.claim: Bloom's 2 sigma result came from short studies on narrow tests that bundled extra time and feedback with tutoring. Later meta-analyses find about one-third SD.
findings.number: Cohen, Kulik and Kulik 1982: 0.33 SD (65 studies); Nickow et al. 2020: 0.37 SD (96 studies); narrow tests 0.84 vs broad tests 0.27 SD
findings.effect_size_or_detail: Bloom's source studies (Anania, Burke) ran for 3 weeks. Mastery learning without tutoring produced about 1.1 SD, so roughly half of the 2 SD came from feedback and testing. Von Hippel's verdict: 'About one-third of a standard deviation seems to be the typical effect' on broad tests. A Chicago programme found 0.06 SD.
findings.source_name: von Hippel, Two-Sigma Tutoring: Separating Science Fiction from Science Fact, Education Next (2024)

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of PreK-12 tutoring experiments finds a large but not 2-sigma effect.
findings.number: Pooled effect 0.37 SD
findings.effect_size_or_detail: Effects are larger with teacher or paraprofessional tutors than with volunteers or parents, larger in earlier grades, and larger in school than after school.
findings.source_name: Nickow, Oreopoulos and Quan, NBER Working Paper 27476 (2020)

findings.claim: Human tutoring and step-based intelligent tutoring systems produce similar effects, both far below 2.0.
findings.number: Human tutoring d = 0.79; intelligent tutoring systems d = 0.76
findings.effect_size_or_detail: Measured against no tutoring. VanLehn notes that answer-based systems, ITS and human tutors were 'believed' to give 0.3, 1.0 and 2.0.
findings.source_name: VanLehn, Educational Psychologist 46(4):197-221 (2011), ERIC abstract

findings.claim: Per-student spending at US public institutions runs into five figures, and instruction alone is $8,000 to $13,500 per FTE.
findings.number: Total expenses per FTE (2020-21): public 4-year $52,900; public 2-year $21,730; private nonprofit 4-year $69,150; for-profit 4-year $17,660. Instruction per FTE: public 4-year $13,540; public 2-year $8,040; private nonprofit 4-year $20,060
findings.effect_size_or_detail: Constant 2021-22 dollars (a footnote on the page says 2020-21 dollars, an inconsistency). Total expenses cover research, hospitals and auxiliaries, so instruction per FTE is the fair comparison.
findings.source_name: NCES Condition of Education, Postsecondary Institution Expenses

findings.claim: Serving static course files costs effectively nothing per extra learner on a free static host.
findings.number: Requests to static assets are 'free and unlimited'; Cloudflare Pages Free plan allows 20,000 files per site, 25 MiB per file and 500 builds per month
findings.effect_size_or_detail: This covers only delivering pages. It does not cover AI tutoring compute, exam fees ($97 per CLEP exam plus proctoring), content authoring or review labour.
findings.source_name: Cloudflare Workers static assets billing; Cloudflare Pages limits

series.title: HarvardX/MITx course completion rate by cohort
series.notes: Table S3. The cohorts overlap. 'Participants' means people who registered and viewed the course.

series.title: Share of the 2012-13 HarvardX/MITx learner cohort still registering in later years
series.notes: Table S1. Later cohorts kept fewer learners: 11.68% of the 2015-16 cohort returned in year two.

series.title: Enrolments vs certifications by country Human Development Index, 2017-18
series.notes: Table S2. HDI is UN 2017. Learners in very-high-HDI countries are over-represented among certificate earners.

series.title: DFW rate before and after OER adoption, University of Georgia
series.unit: percent of final grades that were D, F or W
series.notes: Colvard, Watson and Park 2018, Tables 2-4. Non-randomised pre/post comparison, same instructors, N = 21,822.

series.title: Tutoring effect sizes: Bloom's claim vs later evidence

points.label: Kestin et al. 2025 AI tutor (linear regression, immediate narrow test)
Nickow et al. 2020 PreK-12 tutoring meta-analysis

series.notes: These are not one comparable scale. Test breadth, duration and comparison group differ. VanLehn source: https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ946764 ; Kestin: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12179260/ ; Nickow: https://www.nber.org/papers/w27476

series.title: Instruction expenses per FTE student, 2020-21
series.notes: The private nonprofit instruction figure is the 2020-21 endpoint of the page's 2010-11 to 2020-21 change ($19,450 to $20,060). For-profit instruction is not reported.

lessons_for_design: Free access is not the bottleneck. MOOC completion stayed near 3 to 6% for six years, so plan for persistence (pacing, deadlines, check-ins, a credential at the end), not just open content.
Paying or committing changes behaviour: verified MOOC learners completed about 46 to 56% of the time. A free design needs a non-monetary commitment device, such as a scheduled exam date.
Measure who actually finishes, by income and country. MOOC certificates went mostly to very-high-HDI, already-educated learners, so report completion by Pell-like and HDI-like subgroup from day one.
Tie every course to a credential employers or colleges already accept (CLEP, DSST, licensing exams). The MOOC failure was partly a failure to turn learning into a credential with labour-market value.
Say plainly that credit by exam is not free: $97 per CLEP exam plus proctoring fees, and each college decides whether to grant credit. Show that cost and the acceptance checks upfront.

Make the AI tutor a scaffold, not an answer machine. The positive RCT used pedagogical prompts, step-by-step scaffolding and pre-written verified solutions. Unrestricted GPT-4 lowered exam scores by 17%.
Ground the tutor in reviewed answer keys. This matches the essay's second-reviewer rule, and it is how Kestin et al. got accuracy.
Test without the AI. Bastani shows practice gains with AI can hide learning losses, so each mastery check should run with assistance off.
Promise about one-third of a standard deviation, not two sigma. Realistic tutoring effects on broad tests are about 0.3 to 0.4 SD.
Keep a human route where possible. Tutor CoPilot shows AI that supports human helpers gives measurable gains for about $20 per tutor per year.
OER evidence supports saving money with equal or slightly better outcomes, mostly for lower-income students. It does not support claims of large learning gains from content alone.
Claim 'near zero marginal cost' only for delivery. Static pages cost effectively nothing per learner, but review labour, exam fees and the learner's own AI compute do not.
caveats: The MOOC Pivot data covers HarvardX and MITx only, not all of edX or Coursera. The authors flag this.
MOOC completion is a contested metric because many registrants never intended to finish. Even so, learners who said they intended to complete finished only 11.5 to 17.7% of the time.
Colvard et al. is a single-institution pre/post study with no randomisation. Instructor engagement changed along with the textbook.

Kestin et al. ran for two weeks in one elite-university course, with immediate narrow post-tests and a ceiling effect. Some authors are also active-learning researchers. Gains may not hold for longer or broader outcomes.
The Bastani et al. figures come from the abstract (via RePEc). The PNAS full text returned 403 and I did not read it. The study was in a single setting (high-school maths).
The College Board CLEP placement study is observational and run by the exam's vendor. CLEP groups are very small (17 to 273 students per exam).
OpenStax savings are self-reported and the method is not shown on the impact page.

NCES total expenses per FTE include research, hospitals and other non-instruction spending. Instruction per FTE is the fairer benchmark. The page is also inconsistent about which constant dollars it uses.

Von Hippel's Education Next piece is a policy-journal critique, not peer-reviewed. The meta-analytic numbers it cites (Cohen, Kulik and Kulik; Nickow et al.) are from peer-reviewed or NBER work, and I opened only the Nickow abstract myself.
Tutoring effect sizes in the series are not directly comparable: test breadth, duration and comparison condition differ.
Hilton 2016 was opened only at the abstract level, and Hilton 2020 only as a partial ERIC abstract.
unconfirmed: Share of MOOC learners who already held a degree (the Penn/Coursera survey's reported 83% with a post-secondary degree, and the HarvardX/MITx two-year report's 61 to 81% with a bachelor's). SSRN and MIT DSpace blocked or rate-limited access, so I did not use these numbers. The degreed-learner point rests only on the authors' qualitative statement in The MOOC Pivot.
Hilton 2020 detailed results (114,419 students across 16 efficacy studies; counts of studies favouring OER) are seen only in search summaries.
Modern States figures (vouchers issued, about 50,000 credit-bearing exams, $59M saved in 2025, 145,000 registrants in 2025). The site blocked automated access.
Annual CLEP volume (for example 456,000 exams in 2022) and the number of colleges granting CLEP credit (about 2,900). No primary College Board figure was found.
Military CLEP participation (about 40,000 per year), from secondary sources only.
Completion of the Coursera-Udemy merger in 2026 and the registered-learner totals for the combined company, reported only in secondary news.
The exact date of 2U's Chapter 11 filing (secondary sources say 25 July 2024). The Crimson article says only 'Thursday'.
Bloom (1984) original paper, not opened; its figures are described through von Hippel and VanLehn.
Cloudflare Pages free-plan bandwidth wording ('unlimited bandwidth') was not found on the pages opened. Only the Workers static-assets 'free and unlimited' requests statement is confirmed.
DSST exam fee and exam count: not researched in this pass.
